description: The atmospheric general circulation model is based on a finite‐difference formulation of the primitive equations of meteorology. Water vapor, liquid and solid water, and atmospheric trace species are advected with a monotonic second‐order finite volume scheme. Physical parameterizations include a turbulent scheme based on the prognostic equation for the turbulent kinetic energy, a mass flux representation of the organized structures of the convective boundary layer called “Thermal Plume Model”, and a parameterization of the cold pools or wakes created below cumulonimbus by the evaporation of convective rainfall. The “episodic mixing and buoyancy sorting” scheme used for deep convection was modified to make the closure and triggering rely on the description of the subcloud vertical motions by thermal plumes and wakes. Regarding convection, we modified the lateral detrainment in the thermal plume model to represent satisfactorily well the transition from stratocumulus to cumulus clouds and introduced a statistical triggering for deep convection. The radiation scheme, inherited from ECMWF, includes the Rapid Radiative Transfer Model (RRTM) code for thermal infrared radiation and an improved six‐band scheme for solar radiation. Cloud cover and cloud water content are computed using a statistical scheme using a lognormal function for deep convection and a bigaussian function for shallow cumulus. Finally, the model includes a representation of gravity waves generated by mountains as well as by convection and fronts.
